objective.text: Avoid bypassing central Gate hooks when replacing a named ability check with inline authorization.

difficulty.rationale: Preserve central hook enforcement when refactoring an authorization call.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: A Gate::before hook denies suspended users for named abilities. A developer replaces Gate::authorize("publish") with Gate::allowIf(fn ($user) => $user->ownsPost). A suspended owner now passes. Which framework distinction explains the regression?

options.text: allowIf temporarily unsuspends the authenticated user before checking ownership.
options.rationale: The method does not mutate the user; the missing hook execution explains the different result.
options.misconception: The method does not mutate the user; the missing hook execution explains the different result.

options.text: Named abilities ignore ownership, while inline abilities always grant owners globally.
options.rationale: The difference is which configured checks execute, not an automatic ownership rule built into all gates.
options.misconception: The difference is which configured checks execute, not an automatic ownership rule built into all gates.

options.text: Inline allowIf does not run the normal before/after authorization hooks.
options.rationale: The inline condition is evaluated through the on-demand path, bypassing the central hooks used for named ability checks.

options.text: The before hook runs twice and the second denial cancels the first.
options.rationale: Inline authorization does not run that hook, and repeated denials would not cancel each other.
options.misconception: Inline authorization does not run that hook, and repeated denials would not cancel each other.
